title: Edmund and the Parish
premise: When a stranger's corpse is found in the marshes outside the parish of Wrenlow dressed entirely in clothes stolen from investigator Beatrix Delacroix's own closet, Beatrix is pulled into a case that should not exist: the death, eleven years ago, of Edmund Vasse, the parish's beloved heir whose drowning was ruled an accident. The stolen clothes belonged to Edmund—Beatrix bought them at his estate auction as a child—and whoever staged the body knows things only a witness could know. As the anniversary dinner approaches and parish loyalties close ranks, Beatrix must reconstruct Edmund's final night from fragments of their own flawless memory, discovering that the 'accident' was witnessed by someone who has spent a decade protecting the guilty. In the end, Beatrix exposes the killer—the parish vicar who drowned Edmund to protect the inheritance of the family that funded his church—but must choose between the truth that will shatter Wrenlow and the loyalty of the one friend who helped cover it up.
about_author: Ulyana Ravensworth is the pen name of a former rural claims adjuster who spent fifteen years documenting other people's losses before turning them into fiction. They write from a converted tithe barn in East Anglia, where they keep meticulous notes on everything—including, they admit, things better forgotten.

chapters.title: The Clothes Make the Corpse
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A jogger finds a body in the marsh; when police call Beatrix to identify the clothing, they recognize every piece—Edmund Vasse's suit, shirt, and shoes from the estate auction of their childhood. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Photographs of Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. At the morgue, Beatrix's photographic memory catalogs details others miss: the clothes are aged artificially, the shoes worn wrong-footed. Someone wanted the dead man mistaken for a ghost. Beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Water
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix reviews the closed file on Edmund Vasse's drowning—ruled accidental, witnessed by four parishioners. The victim is identified as a drifter named Callum Reeve. Beat: the past pressing against the present like water against glass.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix interviews the jogger, Maren Oduya, who insists she saw the body twice—once three days ago, alive, wearing those same clothes. Beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Wrenlow prepares its annual dinner commemorating the Vasse legacy; invitations arrive bearing the family crest. Beatrix is invited—as a child beneficiary of the estate. Beat: being drawn back into a world that remembers them.

chapters.title: The Auction Lot
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, with flashback texture. Beatrix recalls buying lot 47—a boy's memory of a dead heir's wardrobe—and realizes the seller was the vicar, Father Ambrose Pell. Beat: suspicion taking root in nostalgia.

chapters.title: Four Witnesses
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix tracks the original witnesses: the housekeeper Mrs. Tallow, groundskeeper Ivo Brand, Edmund's cousin Sylvie Vasse, and Father Pell. All still live within a mile of the marsh. Beat: a closed circle closing tighter.

chapters.title: Mrs. Tallow's Dust
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The housekeeper receives Beatrix amid immaculate rooms and answers questions with rehearsed smoothness—too smooth. A photograph of Edmund is turned face-down. Beat: grief weaponized into denial.

chapters.title: Ivo's Dogs
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The groundskeeper sics his dogs on Beatrix but relents, muttering that the marsh 'gives back what it's owed.' He saw lights out there last week. Beat: fear disguised as hostility.

chapters.title: Sylvie's Glass
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Edmund's cousin Sylvie, now the estate's heir, pours wine and deflects with charm, but her hands shake when Beatrix mentions the clothes. Beat: guilt or grief? Beatrix can't yet tell.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Sermon
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Sunday service; Father Pell preaches on forgiveness and forgetting, eyes finding Beatrix in the pew. Afterward he warns gently against 'digging where the ground has settled.' Beat: menace wrapped in kindness.

chapters.title: What Memory Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, deep flashback. Eleven years ago, twelve-year-old Beatrix watched Edmund leave the boathouse the night he drowned—and remembers a fifth figure no statement ever mentioned. Beat: the buried witness surfacing.

chapters.title: A Second Body of Evidence
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Callum Reeve's room at the inn is searched by someone before Beatrix arrives; a train ticket to Wrenlow dated the week before Edmund's anniversary. He came deliberately. Beat: the investigation inverts—Reeve was hunting too.

chapters.title: Maren's Second Sighting
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Under pressure, Maren admits she told someone about her sighting—and now someone is watching her cottage. Beatrix offers protection; Maren refuses, terrified of the parish more than the killer. Beat: isolation as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In the derelict boathouse, Beatrix finds a hidden ledger: payments from the Vasse estate to the church, escalating after Edmund's death. The inheritance flowed through holy hands. Beat: motive emerging from arithmetic.

chapters.title: Loyalty of Small Towns
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Shopkeepers go silent; Beatrix's rental car tires are slashed. The parish protects itself. An anonymous note: 'Some cases stay closed.' Beat: the town as antagonist.

chapters.title: Sylvie's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Sylvie summons Beatrix at midnight, drunk, beginning to say 'Edmund wasn't—' before a phone call interrupts. By morning she denies everything. Beat: truth strangled by fear mid-sentence.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The dinner proceeds under crystal and candlelight; Beatrix attends, cataloging every guest. Father Pell proposes a toast to Edmund. Beatrix notices the toast echoes a phrase from the forged scene. Beat: elegance over rot.

chapters.title: Lot 47 Revisited
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix retrieves their childhood purchase records and matches fabric fibers from the corpse's clothes to the exact moth-damage pattern in the auctioned garments—clothes that passed through Pell's hands twice. Beat: evidence clicking into place.

chapters.title: Maren Disappears
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Maren vanishes; her cottage burned selectively—only her statement pages. Beatrix finds her hiding in the marsh hut, alive, having seen the arsonist's silhouette: a cassock. Beat: terror becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Fifth Figure Named
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Cross-referencing memory with the ledger, Beatrix identifies the fifth figure from the boathouse night: young Sylvie, who saw the drowning and was paid in silence via her inheritance. Beat: heartbreak—her friend is both victim and accomplice.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Estate
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix confronts Sylvie, who breaks: Father Pell drowned Edmund when Edmund threatened to expose embezzlement, and Sylvie traded silence for survival. She never knew who killed Reeve. Beat: pity tangled with accusation.

chapters.title: Pell's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Police receive an anonymous dossier framing Beatrix for Reeve's murder—photos of Beatrix at the marsh, the auction receipts, a planted motive. Beatrix is detained. Beat: the hunter caged.

chapters.title: The Cell and the Catalogue
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In custody, Beatrix rebuilds the entire case from memory alone, dictating a timeline to a sympathetic constable. The alibi Pell constructed has one seam: the tide tables. Beat: clarity forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Tide That Lies
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Released on the constable's risk, Beatrix proves Reeve was killed inland and moved at low tide—impossible for the times Pell claims to have been at the church. His alibi is a liturgy schedule. Beat: the trap reversing.

chapters.title: What the Vicar Kept
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Searching the vestry, Beatrix finds Reeve's notebook hidden behind the altar: Reeve was Edmund's illegitimate half-brother, investigating the drowning himself. Pell knew and killed him. Beat: the case becomes personal scripture.

chapters.title: Sylvie's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix asks Sylvie to testify. Sylvie wavers—Pell holds her confession to the cover-up over her head. She agrees, then goes missing before dawn. Beat: loyalty and truth tearing the same person apart.

chapters.title: The Marsh Gives Back
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Searchers find Sylvie's scarf at the waterline; Beatrix refuses to believe it and reads the marsh itself—footprints, reed bends—deducing she's held in the old ice house. Beat: memory as survival skill.

chapters.title: The Ice House
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix finds Sylvie bound but alive and springs the trap: constables hidden nearby as Pell arrives to finish his work. He comes, unhurried, in his cassock. Beat: dread crystallizing into confrontation.

chapters.title: Confession at Knife's Edge
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Trapped, Pell speaks freely—he drowned Edmund as 'a mercy to the parish,' killed Reeve as 'a mercy to the past,' and considers Beatrix 'a mercy pending.' Officers move; Pell takes Sylvie hostage toward the water. Beat: evil articulate and calm.

chapters.title: The Water Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. At the boathouse, Pell forces everyone to reenact Edmund's drowning; Beatrix uses their perfect memory of the night—tide, moonlight, the loose plank—to turn his own stage against him. Ivo's dogs bring him down. Beat: climax; the past physically reclaiming him.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Pell confesses fully in custody, almost relieved. Sylvie faces charges for the cover-up but cooperates. The parish learns its saint was a murderer. Beat: hollow victory, air after drowning.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Cost
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix visits Mrs. Tallow, who admits she suspected for years and said nothing because the parish was all she had. Forgiveness is offered and refused, both gently. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Estate Settles
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The Vasse inheritance is unwound; Sylvie, awaiting sentencing, signs the estate to a memorial fund for Edmund and Reeve both. Beatrix declines any share. Beat: restitution without redemption.

chapters.title: Maren's Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Maren testifies despite her fear, and the parish that shunned her begins, awkwardly, to thank her. She and Beatrix share tea—an unlikely friendship. Beat: visibility chosen, finally safe.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix writes the report that officially reopens and closes the Vasse case, every detail verified against their memory. The constable asks how they can be sure. 'I never forget,' Beatrix says, 'that's the problem.' Beat: bittersweet mastery.

chapters.title: The Anniversary, Again
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. One year later, the dinner is held again—smaller, honest, with two names toasted instead of one myth. Beatrix attends by choice. Beat: ritual corrected, community bruised but breathing.

chapters.title: A Letter in Lot 47
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Among returned estate papers, Beatrix finds a letter Edmund wrote before dying, naming his fears—proof he knew Pell was stealing. It ends: 'If anyone reads this, remember me rightly.' Beat: the dead given voice.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix boxes the case files but keeps one thing: the letter, and a photograph of Edmund alive. For the first time, they choose which memories to carry. Beat: quiet transformation.

chapters.title: The Next Case Waits
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A new envelope arrives—another impossible detail, another town's secret. Beatrix hesitates, then opens it, knowing invisibility was always an illusion. Final beat: the investigator walks toward the next truth, eyes open.
